title: xray: the :rf/xray frame logs :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded at each consumer app boot (seen in the rf2-oyr9f tutorial walk)
description:
Claim to reproduce before fixing: a clean consumer app built from the Resources tutorial (rf2-oyr9f, PR #9838: re-frame2 with the -reagent, -routing, -http, -resources and -schemas artefacts, day8/re-frame2-xray under the :dev alias, shadow-cljs 3.4.10 watch) logs :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded from the Xray frame (:rf/xray) at EACH app boot. The worker saw it in the browser console during its walk, did not investigate, and it did not break the walk.

Prior art, all CLOSED, so this is either a regression or a new trigger:
- rf2-chs7: :rf.xray/epoch-recorded floods the :rf/xray queue under load.
- rf2-88f1: the Story shell dispatches into :rf/xray directly and races the seat at boot.
- rf2-avi7: set-target-frame reads a destroyed target frame epoch history.
Read their close reasons first (bd show <id> --json, field close_reason).

Acceptance:
- Reproduce on a minimal consumer (or the in-repo realworld_resources example with Xray in :dev), and name the event whose cascade exceeds depth.
- If it reproduces: a RED-then-GREEN regression and the smallest fix inside tools/xray, with no change to the drain-depth limit itself unless the cause is shown to be legitimate depth.
- If it does NOT reproduce at trunk: close with the exact setup and the clean console as evidence.
Browser work: take the machine-wide shadow-cljs exclusive at dispatch.
notes:
MAYOR DISPATCH NOTE (mayor, 2026-09-15 00:32:30 AUSEST): dispatched to worker/xraybootdrain-a (worktree <HOME>/code/re-frame2-worktrees/xraybootdrain-a, based on d9a7290fef). The fleet was otherwise empty and the machine-wide browser exclusive was free, so this worker holds it.

Scope, reproduce first:
- Reproduce on the in-repo :examples/realworld-resources build (or the tutorial consumer shape), then name the cascade and discriminate: a rf2-chs7 coalescing regression, a boot path coalescing never covered, or a misattributed record (the rf2-avi7 lesson).
- Fix only inside tools/xray, RED then GREEN, without touching the drain-depth limit.
- If the cause is outside Xray, stop and report.
- "Does not reproduce at trunk", with evidence, is a complete result.

Sites verified: install.cljs :75-171 (the coalesced drain and trace listener), epoch.cljs :119-151, spine.cljs :846-880. The prior-art close reasons are intact: rf2-chs7 1327 chars, rf2-88f1 502, rf2-avi7 1447.
WORKER VERDICT (xraybootdrain-a, 2026-09-15 AUSEST): REPRODUCED, CAUSE IN XRAY, FIXED in PR #9839 (draft until the worker marks it ready).

Reproduction (in-repo, no consumer copy needed): `:examples/realworld-resources` compiled with the Xray preload merged in (`--config-merge '{:devtools {:preloads [day8.re-frame2-xray.preload]}}'`), booted headless with a `[data-rf-xray-host]` layout host added to its page. Result: exactly ONE `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` per boot, 3 of 3 boots, `{:frame :rf/xray :depth 100 :queue-size 42 :last-event-id :rf.xray/note-sensitive-suppressed}`. All 16 `:tail-event-ids` were `:rf.xray/note-sensitive-suppressed`. The dropped ids were 27 more of those plus 15 `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/set-width`. The shipped page (no layout host, shell never mounts) logged 0 of 3. That matches the rf2-oyr9f walk's own note, which recorded the error dropping note-sensitive-suppressed events.

The cascade, from runtime instrumentation rather than message text:
- ALL 126 suppressed events were `:rf.sub/run` for XRAY'S OWN subs (`:rf.xray/*`, `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/*`, `:rf.xray.column-widths/*`), each FRAMELESS and `:sensitive? true`, all inside one synchronous `mount-shell-into!` call.
- Stack: Xray shell view -> fresco collector `sub` -> `cold-read!` -> `re-frame.subs/compute-sub*` -> `trace/emit!` -> Xray `collect-trace!` -> privacy gate -> `config/note-suppressed!` -> one dispatch per read into `:rf/xray`.
- Core is behaving as documented. Render-time emits outside any event run stay frameless (Spec 009 Frame identity, `stamp-frame`), and core's sub-tag classification fails a frameless read closed to sensitive.
- Xray's `self-noise/xray-internal-event?` recognises Xray's own traces by frame alone, so these reached the privacy gate and were counted as redacted host events.
- The host's 39 sub-runs on the same boot carried `:rf/default` and were not sensitive.

Candidates discriminated:
- (a) rf2-chs7 epoch-coalescing regression: NO. No `:rf.xray/epoch-recorded` appears in the tail or the dropped ids.
- (b) An uncovered boot path: YES for the amplifier. `note-suppressed!` is a per-event dispatch stream rf2-chs7 never touched.
- (c) Misattribution: YES for the trigger. The burst is Xray's own reads arriving frameless, not the host app's boot.

Why not coalesce `note-suppressed!`: `tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md` states "every atom bump fires a matching dispatch", and coalescing would still have counted 126 phantom redactions.

Fix (tools/xray only): `collect-trace!`'s self-noise branch also drops a trace whose `:rf.sub/id` is in Xray's reserved namespace, via the existing `self-noise/xray-internal-event-id?`. The drain-depth limit is untouched.

Regression: `sensitive_trace_loop_cljs_test.cljs` section (5), committed before the fix, drives the real `rf.trace/emit!` path. It was red on unfixed code: suppressed count 126, `:rf/xray` queue moved from 1 to 127. It is green after the fix. Its control, a host frameless sub read, is still counted.

Control: the fix's one `or` arm was planted as `false` from a clean committed tree. The regression went red again and the boot error came back 3 of 3. The file was restored and verified by committed blob hash.

Gates, all passing locally:
- node-test: 12125 tests / 60452 assertions.
- browser-test: 1106 tests / 6045 assertions.
- Xray feature-gate smoke: 5 scenarios.
- story play-scripts: 31 play rows, 0 unexpected outcomes.
- xray-manual-epoch: 2 tests.
- jvm-tools-xray: 1282 tests.
- clj-kondo and splint clean; require-alias and the tools-rooted ratchets pass; xray-spec-check passes.
- `examples_compile` and `mcp_conformance` were left to CI.

Follow-ups, not filed (the mayor routes):
1. `tools/xray/spec/013-Trace-Consumer.md` lists two self-noise residual classes; this adds a third (frameless Xray sub traces keyed on sub-id namespace). The spec is incomplete rather than wrong.
2. `note-suppressed!` still dispatches once per suppressed HOST event, per spec 015. A genuine host burst of more than 100 frameless sensitive traces in one task would still pass the depth cap. Changing that is a spec decision.
WORKER DONE (mayor, 2026-09-15 01:39:01 AUSEST): worker reported done; PR #9839 is ready, head f8fce1f9a2 on base 3194e220d0, 2 files (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/trace_collector.cljs and test sensitive_trace_loop_cljs_test.cljs). It merges on the criterion. Close this bead on merge.

REPRODUCED: :examples/realworld-resources with the Xray preload merged on the command line (shadow-cljs.edn untouched), in headless Chromium serving a byte-verified compile, gave exactly 1 :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded per boot in 3 of 3 boots: {:frame :rf/xray :depth 100 :last-event-id :rf.xray/note-sensitive-suppressed}, source config.cljc:868 note-suppressed!.

CAUSE (discriminated from evidence): all 126 suppressed traces were :rf.sub/run for Xray OWN subs, frameless (render-time emit outside an event run, per Spec 009) and so sensitive by default, fired inside one synchronous mount-shell-into!. self-noise/xray-internal-event? recognised Xray traces by FRAME only, so they reached the privacy gate, and note-suppressed! dispatched once per trace into :rf/xray. rf2-chs7 regression REFUTED (no epoch-recorded in the tail). This is an uncovered amplifier with a self-misattributed trigger.

FIX: one or-arm in collect-trace! using the existing xray-internal-event-id? on :rf.sub/id. Coalescing was ruled out by spec 015; the drain-depth limit is untouched. The regression went RED (126 suppressed, queue 1 -> 127) then GREEN, with a control that a host sub frameless read is still counted. The plant control re-reddened the test AND brought the boot error back in 3/3; the restore verified by blob hash. Full node-test 12125 / 60452, browser 1106, jvm-tools-xray 1282, feature-gate smoke, 0 failures.

FOLLOW-UPS:
- (1) tools/xray/spec/013-Trace-Consumer.md lists two self-noise classes; this adds a third. Filed as a truth-up bead blocked by this one.
- (2) SPEC QUESTION, not filed: note-suppressed! still dispatches once per suppressed HOST event, as spec 015 requires, so a genuine host burst of >100 frameless sensitive traces in one task would still hit the depth cap. Changing that is a spec decision; surfaced to Mike.

dependencies.title: story: the shell dispatches into Xray's :rf/xray frame directly, and races the seat at boot (residual 2 of rf2-avi7)
dependencies.description:
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:406 hand-rolls (rf/with-frame :rf/xray (rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.xray/set-target-frame now])) — reaching into ANOTHER TOOL'S frame instead of calling Xray's host-facing facade day8.re-frame2-xray.core/set-target-frame!.

Two consequences.

(1) THE MEASURED ONE. rf2-avi7 (PR #9312) seats :rf/xray on substrate-adapter readiness, from the Xray preload's bounded 50ms poll. Measured on one tree carrying both #9312 and #9306, against the same tree with #9312 reverted: 97 :rf.error/frame-destroyed -> 2. The residual 2 fire at t=546.9ms and t=561.9ms on one page — inside the poll window, because Story's boot does rf/init! then mounts the shell and selects a variant before the next tick. Record (captured with a pr-str diagnostic planted in error_emit/report-unowned-error!, restored, blob cf828e0e6c167fd0d421c32de0e3b148f2b8e811 verified):
  {:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed :event :rf/redacted :event-id :rf.xray/set-target-frame :frame :rf/xray :source-coord {:ns day8.re-frame2-xray.epoch :line 108}}
No Xray-side change reaches this: the dispatch is Story's, and by the time the watcher fires rf/init! HAS run — so a facade call would seat successfully and land.

(2) THE STRUCTURAL ONE, which is the real point. A host is not supposed to know that :rf/xray is Xray's frame, nor that its lifecycle is tied to adapter readiness. Story already uses the facade for the sibling gesture (rf.story.xray-preset/on-variant-selected!, wire-cross-host!) and already has the ensure-before-dispatch pattern for its OWN frames (ensure-variant-frame!, rf2-zme7). This one call site is the exception.

PROPOSED (not ruled): (a) Story calls (xray-core/set-target-frame! now) in place of the with-frame + dispatch-sync; (b) Xray's core/set-target-frame! routes through mount/ensure-xray-frame! before dispatching, so the facade is correct at boot instant for EVERY host, not just Story. Both halves are one-liners. (b) alone does not fix Story; (a) alone leaves the facade wrong for the next host.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: npm run test:story-feature-load is a per-PR gate (test.yml, story_full_gate) and PR #9306 turns it red by removing the Story shell's page-wide no-op :errors listener that was masking these. #9312 takes it from 101 console errors to 6; this bead is 2 of the remaining 6. The other 4 are a separate defect — see the sibling bead on :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded.

The two repaired call sites do land the boot dispatch, but core/set-target-frame! now calls mount/ensure-seated!, NOT ensure-xray-frame! as the close reason says. That deliberately leaves first-mount hooks pending. When first open later invokes ensure-xray-frame!, mount.cljs:735-747 unconditionally derives seed-frame from the head focusable bundle (or nil for an empty ring) and dispatch-syncs set-target-frame, overwriting the explicit target already accepted from the host. epoch.cljs:110-117 clears target-frame and focus/frame on nil. A bundle from another frame replaces it with that other frame instead. The new the-facade-seat-does-not-burn-the-first-mount-seed test exercises the first-open edge but only asserts the seeded-frame-ids sentinel, never the surviving target.

dependencies.title: xray: :rf.xray/epoch-recorded floods :rf/xray's own queue under load — 4 :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded in the Story feature-load gate
dependencies.description:
Found while measuring rf2-avi7 (PR #9312). SEPARATE DEFECT — identical count with and without #9312, so it is neither caused nor fixed by that change, and it is NOT the frame-destroyed category rf2-avi7 is about.

npm run test:story-feature-load emits 4 :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded console errors, all on :frame :rf/xray, all from Xray's own instrumentation loop. Two shapes (captured via a pr-str diagnostic planted in error_emit/report-unowned-error!, restored, blob cf828e0e6c167fd0d421c32de0e3b148f2b8e811 verified):

  {:error :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded :frame :rf/xray :depth 100 :queue-size 101
   :last-event-id :rf.xray/epoch-recorded
   :dropped-event-ids [<101 x :rf.xray/epoch-recorded>]
   :tail-event-ids    [<16 x :rf.xray/epoch-recorded>]
   :rollback? false :recovery :no-recovery}

  {:error :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded :frame :rf/xray :depth 100 :queue-size 1
   :last-event-id :rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width
   :dropped-event-ids [:rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width]
   :tail-event-ids [<9 x :rf.xray/epoch-recorded> <7 x :rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width>]}

MECHANISM (to confirm): preload/install-epoch-listener! dispatches :rf.xray/epoch-recorded into :rf/xray on EVERY epoch the framework records, on ANY frame. The gate's 20-event load burst produces epochs faster than :rf/xray's drain settles, so the queue passes the depth-100 cap and the router drops events with :recovery :no-recovery. The second shape shows an unrelated Xray chrome event (edn-inspector/clear-width) being the one dropped because the queue was already full of epoch-recorded — i.e. the flood costs Xray its OWN UI events, not just redundant refreshes.

Note the handler is already a cheap conditional re-read ((if (= frame-id target) (assoc db :epoch-history …) db)) — so for every frame that is NOT the target this is a full dispatch round-trip to compute . Coalescing is the obvious direction, and there is precedent in the same namespace: :rf.xray/sync-trace-buffer is deliberately task-coalesced (rf2-wq6gx) for exactly this reason — 'so the sub fires on every push without one dispatch per trace event'. epoch-recorded never got the same treatment.

PROPOSED (not ruled): coalesce :rf.xray/epoch-recorded the way sync-trace-buffer is coalesced, and/or drop the dispatch entirely for a frame-id that is not the current :target-frame (the listener can read the target without entering the queue).

dependencies.description:
The Resources tutorial does not currently describe one application that a new consumer can build and test through all five chapters. Repair the existing guide as a coherent path; no new Resources API or implicit cache-scope rule is needed.

The namespace at line 60 requires re-frame.http.managed. A detached consumer with exactly the shown dependencies fails to require it; adding only the HTTP artifact succeeds. dependencies.title: xray: :rf.xray/set-target-frame reads a DESTROYED target frame's epoch history, emitting :rf.error/frame-destroyed once per Story variant mount
dependencies.description:
Discovered by rf2-kuky.18 (PR #9306), which removed the Story shell's page-wide no-op :errors listener. That claim had been MASKING these errors; with it gone they reach the console and `npm run test:story-feature-load` is RED at 8 console errors (a PR gate, test.yml:4127).

They are XRAY's, not Story's. A diagnostic :errors listener captured all eight records, identical in shape:

  {:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed
   :event-id :rf.xray/set-target-frame
   :frame :rf/xray
   :source-coord {:ns day8.re-frame2-xray.epoch
                  :file "tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/epoch.cljs" :line 108}}

MECHANISM. Xray holds a STALE TARGET FRAME across a Story variant switch. The :rf.xray/set-target-frame handler (epoch.cljs:108) evaluates (rf/epoch-history target) where target is the previously observed frame; Story has destroyed it, so the read recover-but-emits :rf.error/frame-destroyed. Once per variant mount, 8 across the feature-load run. The record is attributed to :frame :rf/xray, which is ALIVE - the destroyed frame is the READ TARGET, not the record's owning frame.

WHY THE rf2-kuky.18 SINK ARM CANNOT COVER IT. The new console-fallback predicate owns a record when its frame routed it to a registered :observability :errors sink. route-frame? is false for EVERY frame-destroyed emission (rf2-bf0io, so a dead incarnation's bare id can never resolve to a same-id successor's sink), so the route is suppressed and the delivered-count is necessarily 0. Giving :rf/xray an :observability :errors policy would NOT silence these. The fix has to be in Xray.

LIKELY FIX (not ruled). Either clear/repoint :target-frame when the targeted frame is destroyed, or guard the (rf/epoch-history target) read against an unresolved frame. The general case matters beyond Story: any app that destroys a frame Xray is targeting hits this. Do NOT fix it from the Story side - that would paper over it at the wrong layer and leave the general case broken.

SCOPE. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/epoch.cljs plus the tools/xray/spec update every Xray dispatch carries. Needs a regression test.

SEQUENCING. PR #9306 should not merge until this lands, because test:story-feature-load is a per-PR gate and #9306 turns it red by revealing this.
dependencies.notes:
WORKER xrayepoch-a, 2026-09-05. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9312 (open, ready for review). Branch worker/xrayepoch-a, rebased onto ba9b78acb1.

THIS BEAD DIAGNOSED THE WRONG MECHANISM. The description says Xray "reads (rf/epoch-history target) against the destroyed frame" and that "the record is attributed to :rf/xray, which is alive". Both halves are refuted at source, and the second is backwards.

REFUTATION AT SOURCE. rf/epoch-history -> re-frame.core-epoch/epoch-history (a defwrapper with :on-absent :empty-vec) -> late-bind :epoch/epoch-history -> re-frame.epoch/epoch-history -> re-frame.epoch.state/history-for, whose whole body is (or (get @histories frame-id) []). It consults NO frame registry, so it cannot raise :rf.error/frame-destroyed for any target, destroyed or otherwise.

WHERE THE RECORD ACTUALLY COMES FROM. router/emit-frame-destroyed! stamps :frame with the DISPATCH TARGET ((:frame envelope)), and error-emit/error-source-coord resolves a frame-destroyed :source-coord out of the [:event id] registry — i.e. the reg-event registration line. So {:frame :rf/xray, :event-id :rf.xray/set-target-frame, :source-coord epoch.cljs:108} reads: a dispatch of :rf.xray/set-target-frame into :rf/xray was rejected because :rf/xray IS THE MISSING FRAME. The coord names the handler, not the caller — which is exactly what made the record look like an epoch.cljs bug.

MEASURED, three-way probe on the node-test runner (probe deleted before the PR opened):
  A  :rf/xray ALIVE, read target DESTROYED  -> [] , nothing emitted   <- the bead claim, refuted
  B  :rf/xray ABSENT                        -> the exact field-report record
  C  :rf/xray DESTROYED                     -> the exact field-report record

THE REAL GENERAL CASE. Xray registers its whole :rf.xray/* instruction set at preload, but :rf/xray was created by open! — a React commit. In between, Xray is ADDRESSABLE BUT NOT WRITABLE: any dispatch into it recovers-but-emits, drops the host intent, and misattributes the diagnostic. A host that sets :rf.xray/auto-open? false (both Story testbeds do, in their run fns) never leaves that window until it opens a panel.

THE FIX. :rf/xray genuinely cannot be seated at preload LOAD time — rf/make-frame goes through rf.substrate.adapter/make-state-container, which raises :rf.error/no-adapter-installed with no adapter; that is what rf2-e9s81 reverted, and it is about the ADAPTER, not about opening. The preload already runs a bounded readiness loop watching for adapter install, so the seat moved there. auto-open-inline! -> boot-on-runtime-ready!; the open is now the conditional half. The first-mount seed/hydrate fan-out stays lazy behind seeded-frame-ids. Statement: Xrays frame exists as soon as the host runtime does, not when its UI opens. NOT a guard on the epoch read — probe A shows there is nothing there to guard, and a guard would have left the dropped-dispatch general case untouched while looking fixed.

EFFECT ON THE GATE, measured on ONE tree carrying both this change and #9306, against the SAME tree with this commit reverted (git revert, an exact counterfactual rather than a hand-plant):
  reverted:  97 frame-destroyed + 4 drain-depth-exceeded = 101 console errors, exit 1
  fixed:      2 frame-destroyed + 4 drain-depth-exceeded =   6 console errors, exit 1
Removed AT SOURCE, not masked: the regression test asserts the dispatch lands and core/target-frame reads back :app/main.

#9306 IS NOT UNBLOCKED BY THIS PR ALONE. The remaining 6 are two other defects, both outside this bead fence and both filed:
  rf2-88f1 (P2) — the residual 2. Story shell.cljs:406 hand-rolls (rf/with-frame :rf/xray (rf/dispatch-sync ...)) into another tools frame in the same breath as rf/init!, at t=546.9ms / t=561.9ms, inside the readiness polls 50ms window. No Xray-side change reaches it.
  rf2-chs7 (P2) — the 4 drain-depth-exceeded. Xrays own :rf.xray/epoch-recorded fan-out floods :rf/xray queue (:queue-size 101, :depth 100) under the 20-event load; identical count in BOTH columns, so pre-existing and unrelated.
